versioning_decision: Released as 26.10.4 under mandatory YY.MM.VV scheme

findings.baseline: Gate G used reference-results as the default qualification input although the eval README stated they were evaluator fixtures only.
findings.risk: A fixture PASS could be misread as live provider/model behavioral evidence.
findings.remediation: Reference fixtures require explicit --fixture-mode; live qualification requires a typed BehavioralQualificationEvidence manifest and captured-result hashes.

findings.baseline: SABSA-to-EA projection was JAI-native, but direct SABSA Markdown authoring did not persist canonical JAI identity/profile metadata.
findings.risk: SABSA source objects remained a partially parallel write representation.
findings.remediation: New/modified/migrated local SABSA elements now persist canonical_ref, jai_profile, jai_layer and jai_release; the library declares JAI semantic identity authority.

findings.baseline: Runtime agent/policy JAI bindings existed as side registries and ExecutionRecord did not itself carry JAI L6 binding.
findings.risk: Runtime evidence could be structurally valid without proving its JAI responsibility boundary.
findings.remediation: Agent contracts embed and runtime-enforce JAI bindings, managed policy declares its runtime profile, and ExecutionRecord is a typed JAI L6 record.

findings.baseline: ProjectionManifest v3 carried lineage, but publication.py render could be called directly without a manifest.
findings.risk: A production-looking render could bypass projection completeness and lineage controls.
findings.remediation: Production render now requires a matching ProjectionManifest v3 and emits render-evidence.json with output hashes and QA results.

findings.baseline: 26.10.3 was the sole native write namespace and had no forward migration into the new GA release.
findings.risk: Renumbered Unified Lifecycle GA could create compatibility drift.
findings.remediation: 26.10.4 schema namespace and deterministic 26.10.3->26.10.4 migration added; 26.10.0-26.10.3 remain read/migrate compatible.

findings.baseline: EA writes were profile-native, but repository.py only accepted legacy schema_version 26.10 in addition to the current 26.10.3 value.
findings.risk: A repository persisted by 26.10.3 would be rejected after advancing the package version instead of upgrading on write.
findings.remediation: 26.10.4 accepts 26.10, 26.10.1, 26.10.2 and 26.10.3 repository schema versions for read/migrate and writes only 26.10.4. The EA repository-model schema now references the 26.10.4 release namespace.

preserved_from_26.10.3: EA scoped authority and Open Exchange interoperability
